title: Marketplace launch asset QA slate and tone guide
summary: Working slate for marketplace tile + listing copy, acceptance QA checklist, tone guide for partner-facing copy, and a compact runbook for launch readiness. Meant to be lightweight reference the product/partner/creative teams can iterate on quickly.
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic checklist + tone guide to accelerate partner marketplace launches. It's intentionally lightweight — assume commercial/tech/legal signoffs tracked elsewhere (linked artifacts). Use this doc during final asset reviews and the preflight standup before publish.

Context and constraints (notes to self):
- Target marketplace: AWS Marketplace first, then Azure/GCP variants.
- Tile imagery must avoid screenshots containing customer PII. Use abstract GPU/edge illustration.
- SKU mapping: single entitlements SKU for self-serve, separate for enterprise bundle. Confirm with billing.
- Deadline: partner signoff + security review 5 business days before go-live.

Quick launch acceptance gates (stoplight checks):
- Copy: headline, 1-sentence subhead, 3 bullets on value props, 2 sample use-cases — passed if no more than 12 edits remain.
- Legal: approved EULA excerpt and privacy pointer — green if legal stamp on Confluence exists.
- Tech: working provisioning flow verified in staging with demo account — green if provisioning + SSO succeed.
- Observability: basic telemetry (install, license assignment, first API call) instrumented and tested in staging.
- Security: KMS/KV handling confirmed (for private deployments); SOC/Audit checklist items resolved.
- Creative: tile, hero, favicon sized and compressed per marketplace specs.

Checklist: copy and content
- Headline (12–60 chars): gets to the value prop (e.g., "Low-latency LLM inference for production"). Draft variants: A/B test later.
- Subhead (1 short sentence): target developer/platform buyer. Avoid vendor buzzwords-only.
- 3 bullets (benefits, not features): latency, cost predictability, deployment modes. Keep each < 140 chars.
- Use cases (2): short one-liners that read well in tile card ("Customer support summarization") + one enterprise example ("PCI-compliant private deployment").
- CTA copy: "Get started" for free-tier, "Contact sales" if enterprise SKU present.
- Long description (up to 1,000 chars): include model compatibility, SLA summary, and quick setup bullets.
- Technical bullet list: supported models, quantization options, region coverage. Keep concise.
- Compliance/Certs: list only finalized items with links to cert PDFs in Confluence.
- Pricing summary: high-level statement and link to detailed pricing doc. No raw prices unless marketplace requires.

Tone guide (short):
- Audience: engineers (primary), procurement/platform leads (secondary).
- Voice: pragmatic, specific, and slightly technical. Avoid fluff and hyperbole.
- Do use: concrete metrics (latency ms, tokens/sec), example workloads.
- Don't use: "best-in-class"/"world-leading" without measurable claim.
- Inclusivity: avoid vertical-specific claims unless partner approved for that vertical.

Creative & asset specs
- Tile (square): 1200x1200 PNG, export @2x. Keep text minimal (logo + 6-word strapline).
- Hero (landscape): 1600x900 JPG optimized. Use abstract illustration, avoid real faces.
- Icon/fav: 512x512 PNG and 128x128 PNG.
- File naming convention: partnername_tile.png; partnername_hero.jpg; partnername_logo.svg.
- Color palette: follow Redwoods brand palette for overlays; partner accent allowed by CS.

Technical QA (must-pass test cases):
- Provisioning smoke test: create trial tenant via marketplace flow => confirm tenant ID, billing tag, and first-token success in staging logs.
- Version pin: confirm requested model version resolves in runtime and fallback path exists.
- Region fallback: simulate N+1 region failure and confirm traffic reroutes to backup model/region per policy.
- Metrics: verify that token_count, request_latency_ms, error_rate emitted to telemetry sink.
- Security: SAML/SSO flow exercise (if applicable) and secrets rotation check.

Operational runbook snippets (short):
- Pre-publish: final asset ZIP (copy + images + long description + legal link + SKU mapping) to shared artifacts in GitHub release.
- Post-publish quick checks (0–48h): monitoring dashboard for usage, error spikes, and provisioning failures. Daily standup note if >2% error rate.
- Rollback: if provisioning fails at scale, unpublish tile and revert traffic to trial plan; notify partner team and legal.

Common lightweight copy examples (variants to iterate in place):
1) Headline: "Production LLM inference — <partner> on Redwood"
   Subhead: "Deploy low-latency models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
   Bullets: "Predictable per-token economics", "Autoscaled GPU pools for bursts", "Out-of-the-box caching and batch optimization"

2) Headline: "Ship chat & generation features faster"
   Subhead: "SDKs and turnkey runtime that keep latency low and cost predictable."
   Bullets: "Developer-friendly API & SDKs", "Telemetry and CTA-ready dashboards", "Model version pinning and rollouts"

Unresolved questions / decisions to make (flagged for partner sync):
- Do we include a 30-day free trial SKU or only a dev-tier with credits? (Billing decision)
- Any vertical-specific claims (health/finance) require legal review — is partner cleared?
- Which Confluence page will host the compliance PDFs? link to include in final description.

Launch timeline (example mini-sprint):
- T minus 12 days: creative drafts complete
- T minus 9 days: legal + security review started
- T minus 7 days: technical staging verification
- T minus 3 days: go/no-go with partner and CS
- T minus 0: publish (monitor first 72h)

Notes to reviewer (Maya):
- This doc is intentionally opinionated and small — use it for the final sprint checklist.
- Remove any raw pricing numbers unless marketplace requires.
- If partner asks for multi-tenant examples in tile copy, escalate to product for a short approval cycle.

Appendix: quick copy QAs (things to scan for during review)
- Avoid superlatives without metric.
- Check verbs: prefer "deploy"/"scale"/"observe" vs marketing verbs.
- Accessibility: alt text for hero must be provided (1–2 sentences).
- Attachments: include governance acceptance (legal stamp) as asset in the final ZIP.

End of slate.
